posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
The number of plugins written for MV that work with MZ surprised me.
I am fairly new to MZ and stand to be corrected, but it seems to me that the biggest thing that FOSSIL does is to let you use plugin commands for MV plugins.
Perhaps the message telling you that the plugin is not intended for MZ and might not work properly has something to do with the fact that plugins written for MZ seem to have a line "* @target MZ" near the beginning of the help/comment section? I will have to try and find out next time I have another go at plugin writing.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
It really depends on what the plugin does. There are some parts of the engine that are almost the same between MV and MZ, and there are some parts that are quite different.
FOSSIL does allow you to use MV commands in MZ. It's possible to do that even without FOSSIL though. It's a bit difficult to pull off (you have to create a project in MV, make an event that uses a plugin command, then migrate the project to MZ so you can copy-paste that plugin command), but it can be done.
FOSSIL also provides some portability for parts of the engine that
are
incompatible. One big example of this is the window system – any MV plugin that modifies the UI is quite unlikely to work in MZ without FOSSIL. I'm not sure if there are other such areas, but the battle system is
likely
one, given that there's an entirely new battle system option in MZ.
You are also correct that the
@target MZ
line is what informs MZ that a plugin is compatible with it. I wouldn't really recommend adding it to an MV plugin to silence the warning, however.
(All of the above also means that in some cases it's possible to take a plugin written for MZ and use it in MV. I've done that once or twice myself.)
